divergence_justification: Judge accepted the contested divergence: mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_chartevents.sql:9 casts source charttime through TIMESTAMPTZ and line 67 writes the transformed value to Observation.effectiveDateTime. Thus MIN(transform(charttime)) differs from transform(MIN(charttime)) across spring-forward gaps, accounting for seven intime_hr aggregate conflicts; the one outtime_hr conflict is directly replay-attributed to the same cast. All 8/73,181 conflicts (0.011%) are accounted for, and the original 02:mm wall times are unrecoverable from FHIR because effectiveDateTime carries only the normalized value and issued carries storetime. Resource ids are opaque and cannot recover them. The loss changes no row inclusion, stay_id key, grouping, or temporal carry-forward, and is accepted under the contract's proven-DST upstream-defect exemption.

reopen_history.reason: Same Observation.id UUIDv5 inversion as icp. Refused by sql_lint (resource-id-inversion); UTC-pinned reads plus comparator key_attribution make it unnecessary.

Downstream SQL-on-FHIR consumers join derived tables on getResourceKey() resource keys, which the port computes internally but drops at the outermost SELECT. The attempt adds the paired key column beside each MIMIC identifier column (subject_id->patient_key, hadm_id->encounter_key, stay_id->icu_encounter_key, specimen_id->specimen_key). Additive and shape-only: both comparison paths project manifest columns explicitly, so no compared value can change. The MIMIC integer columns are retained as the oracle join keys.

Observation.id is opaque and UUID reconstruction is forbidden.
